newsitem.title: USA: Outlook bleak for Broward Cty, Fla bond vote - paper.
newsitem.headline: Outlook bleak for Broward Cty, Fla bond vote - paper.

text.p: Supporters of a Broward County, Fla., school bond referendum have postponed organizing efforts because a poll suggested it had little chance of passing, the Fort Lauderdale Sun-Sentinel said Wednesday.

The poll conducted for the Friends of Education and Children political action committee was not made public. But the newspaper quoted school board officials who were briefed on the survey as saying the results were "disastrous."
"We have to overcome a negative attitude in the general public's mind," the newspaper quoted school board chairman Abe Fischler as saying.
The board has discussed putting a general obligation bond issue of $350 million to $800 million on the November ballot.

The political action committee opened a campaign account earlier this month to begin promoting the plan. But the newspaper said the group had decided to postpone organizing efforts until the atmosphere improves.

The newspaper said the survey found strong criticism of school board officials, who are perceived as insensitive and unresponsive, and widespread complaints that board members are elected countywide rather than from districts.
In September 1995, Broward County voters overwhelmingly rejected a one-cent sales tax hike to build schools.

The metropolitan Fort Lauderdale district estimates it has $1.4 billion of construction needs through 2002. It already has 33,000 more students than its schools were designed to hold and enrollment is expected to grow by 9,000 students a year through 2001.
